Subject: redlines - MSA & Order Form (brand / press clauses)

Evelyn,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are our redlines to the MSA and Order Form focused on confidentiality and publicity. The key asks from our side:

- No press release mentioning StratusAI without explicit, signed approval per instance.
- Logo use limited to marketing collateral & case studies after a mutual approval cycle (5 business days).
- Reference rights limited to aggregate, non-sensitive metrics; no customer quotes without separate release.
- Confidentiality: extend data retention protections for logs to 24 months and require notification for subpoenas.

We highlighted the problematic clauses in the attached PDF (StratusAI_MSA_Redlines_20270502.pdf) and included a short summary (procurement_notes.docx).

Please confirm next steps and whether Redwood can propose compromise language for press/logo. We're aiming to close the DOCS signature by end of next week.

Subject: Proposed compromise language for publicity & logo use

Olivia / team —

Per Evelyn's note, we've drafted a compromise to address the core of your concerns while keeping reasonable operational guardrails. High level:

1) Press mentions
- Redwood will not issue press releases that reference StratusAI or use StratusAI branding without prior written approval for each release. StratusAI will have up to five (5) business days to review and approve draft copy; approval may be withheld for good reason. For time-sensitive joint product announcements, parties will use a good-faith accelerated review (48 hours) and a post-issue notification requirement.

2) Logo & case-study use
- StratusAI grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable license to reproduce StratusAI’s logo solely for use in Redwood marketing materials, customer lists, and case studies subject to mutual approval. Redwood will provide artwork and final copy for review; StratusAI will respond within five (5) business days.

3) Reference rights / quotes
- Unless a separate release is executed, Redwood may reference StratusAI in aggregate form only and may not attribute customer quotes or sensitive metrics without explicit written consent.

4) Confidentiality & logs
- Redwood proposes a limited retention carve: customer request logs and application-level telemetry related to contract performance will be retained up to 12 months for operational support; access and disclosure will follow subpoena/notice obligations in the MSA. Redwood will notify StratusAI of any compelled disclosures where permitted by law.

Attached: RW_StratusAI_MSA_OrderForm_Compromise_20270505.docx with inline redlines.

If this aligns, we can route the compromise to Legal for final redline next week. Goal: lock commercial terms and push to signature.

Cheers,

Dev Patel
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Subject: Final redline — MSA / Order Form (brand & press clauses)

Olivia / LegalOps —

Thanks for the back-and-forth. I reviewed Dev's compromise and made limited, legally-binding clarifications. Key points in the attached PDF (MSA_OrderForm_FinalRedline_20270507.pdf):

- Press approvals: retains 5 business day review, clarifies "silence is not deemed approval" (we left the accelerated 48h option for joint announcements but added a requirement to document approval requests).
- Logo license: narrow scope, revocable on termination; Redwood must remove logo from marketing materials within 10 business days of revocation.
- Quotes & attribution: moved to explicit separate release; added example of acceptable aggregate statements.
- Logs & subpoenas: accepted notification obligation to the extent legally permitted; preserved Redwood's ability to comply with lawful process. We did not accept an across-the-board 24-month retention period for operational logs — proposed 12 months with a data subject-specific escalation path.

Please review the attached final redline and confirm if this is acceptable for StratusAI to sign. If yes, I will prepare the DocuSign envelope and circulate.

If there are any narrow counterpoints, highlight them inline and we will triage.

Regards,

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
